replication.target_description: Study 1: unethical versus ethical recall, comparing choice of antiseptic wipe versus pencil. Introduction explicitly identifies this as a conceptual replication of Zhong and Liljenquist Study 3.

es.location: Printed p. 24, Study 1 Results and Discussion

notes: Identity independently checked: full primary article Is cleanliness next to godliness? Dispelling old wives’ tales: Failure to replicate Zhong and Liljenquist (2006), by Jennifer V. Fayard, Amandeep K. Bassi, Daniel M. Bernstein and Brent W. Roberts; JASNH 2009 Vol. 6 No. 2, printed pp. 21–29, including methods, results, references and receipt dates. Title, authors and journal match the assigned replication reference. No DOI is printed or assigned. This is the primary report of its two studies, not a secondary article or preregistration. No PDF was supplied. Only assigned unfinished fields assessed; all remaining fields are unassigned placeholders. Cohen’s h is not printed. Retained the printed chi-square statistic without conversion. The same-test p is .63; p is unassigned and remains a placeholder.
